context: Rotating orthographic globe showing 30 world cities colored by continent (6 categories) with a day/night terminator, continuous auto-rotation, and hover tooltips.
first_impression: Clean and uncluttered — a single globe with well-spaced dots and a restrained 6-color palette creates low cognitive demand despite the animation.
what_works: The Tol-derived 6-color palette is perceptually distinct and maps cleanly to the legend; with only one view and 30 point marks there is no working memory burden. The subtitle acts as a built-in legend for interactions, and the dark background makes most city dots pop.
what_doesnt: Europe's legend color (#228833 green) nearly disappears against the dark-green land fill (#1a5c3a), making European cities hard to spot without hovering — the primary categorical encoding fails for one of six continents. Additionally, continuous rotation means the terminator line and city positions are never stable, so perceptual evaluation of day/night context requires sustained tracking; static assessment of animation quality is limited.
